title: Deep learning helps prioritize potent MAGL inhibitor candidates
summary: Deep graph neural networks trained on 13,490 Minisci reaction outcomes predicted reaction feasibility for a virtual library of 26,375 compounds derived from moderate MAGL inhibitors. Combined with physicochemical and structure-based scoring, this workflow prioritized 212 candidates; 14 were synthesized and showed subnanomolar MAGL inhibition, with reported potency improvements up to 4,500-fold over the starting hit. This is an AI-assisted, human-selected laboratory optimization result, not an autonomous workflow or a therapeutic outcome.
ai_technology: Deep graph neural networks for reaction outcome prediction; multi-objective molecular optimization

evidence.tested: Fourteen selected synthesized compounds were reported with subnanomolar MAGL inhibition and co-crystal structures for three ligands.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication, clinical activity and version 1 claim correspondence were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Reaction-prediction models trained on high-throughput Minisci experiments contributed to candidate feasibility scoring; other computational scores and human selection also shaped the experimental set.

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v2 abstract and version metadata reviewed; full manuscript and supplements not inspected.
